Given city-year as the unit of analysis, we use the panel data regression model (Allison, 2009).

rationale: Zhou and Liang (2021) examine how China's household registration system (hukou)—specifically the share of urban temporary residents lacking permanent local legal residency registration—is associated with municipal wastewater treatment capacity and volume of wastewater treated per 10,000 persons (alongside solid waste treatment and public green space). The single focal legal-institutional mechanism empirically tested is legal residency/registration status under the hukou regime (eligibility_status_documentation). For WASH-relevant outcomes, the study measures per-capita wastewater treatment plant capacity (10,000 m3/day per 10,000 persons) and annual quantity of wastewater treated per 10,000 persons, classified as effective_access (sanitation treatment service quantity/capacity per capita, though measured at the aggregate prefecture-city municipal provision level rather than household hookups, creating a secondary conceptual boundary with administrative_outcome). The empirical design uses two-way city and year fixed-effects panel regressions (plus lagged and first-differenced specifications) across 290 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2008 to 2014 without exploiting an exogenous policy shock (explicitly stopping before the 2014 hukou reform), making it an observational study.
